title: Clamp the catalog page index when the item list shrinks
body:
## Summary
CatalogGearTab keeps currentPage when the filtered entry count drops for a reason other than a filter change, so the grid can show an empty page with "Page 3 of 2".

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/catalog/CatalogGearTab.tsx:107-108 derive totalPages and slice pageEntries from the raw currentPage. Filter/search changes reset it (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/catalog/CatalogFiltersBar.tsx:46-74 call resetPage), but a store-side shrink (delete/reset/re-seed from another tab, or an Add Item that clears filters while on a later page is fine) does not. When currentPage >= totalPages the grid renders 0 cards while filteredCount > 0, so neither cards nor the empty state show, and src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/catalog/CatalogPagination.tsx:16 prints "Page N+1 of M" with N+1 > M. Fixed: derive page = min(currentPage, max(0, totalPages-1)) and use it for slicing and the pager.

## Flow
- user pages to page 3 of 3 (41+ items)
- items are removed from the catalog store elsewhere until 2 pages remain
- grid shows no cards and no empty state; pager reads "Page 3 of 2"

## Expected impact
Designers never land on a blank grid after a catalog shrink; measured by a render test that shrinks the store while on the last page. Could break nothing visible: page only clamps when out of range.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the grid never renders an out-of-range page
Before: reproduced by reading: page index has 0 clamps; any shrink past the current page renders 0 of filteredCount>0 items
After: predicted 0 out-of-range renders
Method: simulation - walked the three resetPage callers and the store shrink path; a render test needs CatalogGearTab mounted with useModuleCLI/useGeneration mocked, which is an M instrument
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: render test: mount CatalogGearTab with vi.mock(useModuleCLI, useGeneration), page to the last page, delete entries via useCatalogStore, assert cards > 0 and pager text

title: Confirm before Remove tab and Reseed wipe stash placements
body:
## Summary
The spatial stash Remove-tab (trash icon) and Reseed buttons destroy every placement in the active tab on one click, with no confirm and no undo.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/catalog/spatial-stash/SpatialStashSection.tsx:45 calls removeTab(activeTab.id) and :123-132 calls reseedActiveTab directly from onClick. The store is persisted (spatialInventoryStore), so the hand-arranged layout is gone for good. The repo ships a shared destructive-confirm primitive (ui/ConfirmDialog). Fixed: route both through ConfirmDialog naming the tab and its item count.

## Flow
- designer arranges 20 items in Tab 2
- clicks the trash icon next to the tabs (title "Remove active tab")
- the tab and its 20 placements are deleted immediately

## Expected impact
An accidental click no longer erases a layout; measured by a render test asserting removeTab is not called until confirm. Could annoy power users with one extra click.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - destructive stash actions require confirmation
Before: reproduced by reading: 2 of 2 destructive stash actions fire with 0 confirmation
After: predicted 0 of 2 unconfirmed
Method: simulation - read both handlers; the confirm test is S but the ConfirmDialog wiring and copy is a small UX decision
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: render SpatialStashSection with 2 tabs, click Remove, assert tab count unchanged until the ConfirmDialog confirm button is clicked

title: Say why a stash tile rotation was refused
body:
## Summary
Clicking a placed tile's Rotate when the rotated footprint does not fit does nothing at all; the failure branch is an empty block.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/catalog/spatial-stash/SpatialStashGrid.tsx:170-171: movePlacementAction returns false when the rotated footprint collides or leaves the grid, and the if (!ok) block is empty by design ("keep silent on failure"). The user sees a dead button. Fixed: a transient role=status message ("No room to rotate <item> here") or a brief error tint on the tile.

## Flow
- place a 1x3 sword in the bottom row
- click Rotate (needs 3 rows of height)
- nothing happens, no feedback

## Expected impact
Designers learn why rotate did nothing; measured by a render test asserting a status message after a refused rotate. Could add noise if the message is not transient.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a refused rotate is explained
Before: reproduced by reading: 1 of 1 refusal paths silent
After: predicted 0 silent refusals
Method: simulation - read the handler and movePlacement contract; needs a feedback-design choice (toast vs tint)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: render SpatialStashGrid with a tile against the bottom edge, click Rotate, assert a role=status message names the item

title: Give the spatial stash a keyboard path to place and move items
body:
## Summary
Placing an item in the stash is HTML5 drag-and-drop only: palette rows are not focusable and no key places or moves a tile.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/catalog/spatial-stash/SpatialStashPalette.tsx:107-108 renders rows as draggable divs with no tabIndex/role/key handler; src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/catalog/spatial-stash/SpatialStashGrid.tsx:110-121 offers only an "R" rotate keydown that applies during a drag. Keyboard and switch users cannot place, move or re-arrange anything (WCAG 2.1.1). Fixed: focusable palette rows (Enter = pick up), arrow keys move a picked footprint over the grid with the same canPlace preview, Enter drops, Escape cancels.

## Flow
- Tab into the palette
- no row takes focus; nothing can be picked up
- the grid only accepts pointer drops

## Expected impact
The stash becomes operable without a pointer; measured by a keyboard-only render test placing an item. Could regress drag if the shared drag intent is reused carelessly.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - keyboard users can place and move stash items
Before: reproduced by reading: 0 of 3 stash operations (place, move, rotate-in-place via buttons aside) keyboard-operable for placement
After: predicted 3 of 3
Method: simulation - read both components; this is a new interaction mode (L)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: keyboard-only RTL test: focus palette row, Enter, ArrowRight x2, Enter -> placement exists at (2,0)

title: Show sunburst percentages that match the drawn arcs
body:
## Summary
AffixSunburst normalizes each sibling group before drawing, but the labels print the raw authored probability, and ring-2 labels print a conditional share without saying so.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/catalog/AffixSunburst.tsx:50-53 and :63-66 normalize angles by the sibling sum; :59 and :72 print (probability * 100). If an authored group sums to 1.2, the arcs partition the circle while labels add to 120%. Ring-2 labels (e.g. "Power (40%)" under "1 Prefix (50%)") are P(power | 1 prefix), while the arc's share of the whole circle is 20%; nothing says which. Fixed: label with the normalized share, and suffix ring-2 with "of <parent>" (or print the absolute share).

## Flow
- author a tree whose children sum to 1.2
- arcs fill exactly 360 deg; labels read 60% + 60%
- reader cannot reconcile labels with arc sizes

## Expected impact
Labels and arcs agree; measured by a render test on an unnormalized tree. The shipped AFFIX_PROB_TREE sums to 1.0, so today only the conditional-share ambiguity is visible.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every sunburst label equals its arc share
Before: shipped tree: 3 of 3 ring-1 labels agree, 8 of 8 ring-2 labels conditional and unlabelled as such; unnormalized tree: 0 of N agree
After: predicted N of N agree
Method: simulation - read the angle and label code; choosing conditional vs absolute wording is a presentation decision
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: render AffixSunburst on a tree summing to 1.2 and assert the aria-label percentages sum to 100 per ring

title: Make Add Item image slugs unique and non-empty
body:
## Summary
Add Item derives the image path from the name slug alone, so two items with the same name share one public/items/<slug>.webp and a name of only symbols yields "/items/.webp".

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/catalog/CatalogGearTab.tsx:178 slugifies the name; the entity id gets a Date.now() suffix (:185) but imagePath (:192) and the CLI target (createItemPrompt) do not. A second "Frost Blade" overwrites the first one's icon; "!!!" gives slug "" and the agent is told to write public/items/.webp. Fixed: one slug helper that falls back to "item" and appends the same id suffix to the file name.

## Flow
- create item "Frost Blade" and let its icon generate
- create a second "Frost Blade"
- the second generation overwrites the first item's icon file

## Expected impact
Each item owns its icon file; measured by a unit test on the slug helper. Could break: hand-saved icons that rely on the bare-slug naming (none in tree reference user- ids).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every created item has a unique, non-empty image path
Before: by reading: same-name items -> 1 shared path; symbol-only name -> empty slug
After: predicted unique, non-empty for both
Method: simulation - walked both cases through handleCreateItem; touches the prompt helper and the entity path together
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: unit test on an extracted itemSlug(name, id): "!!!" -> non-empty; two same names -> two paths

title: Do not render a broken icon for an item whose image is not generated yet
body:
## Summary
A newly added item renders next/image at /items/<slug>.webp immediately, before the CLI has written it, so the card shows a broken image (and keeps it forever if the CLI run fails).

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/catalog/CatalogGearTab.tsx:192 sets imagePath before generation; src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/catalog/TradingCard.tsx:119 renders <Image> whenever imagePath is set, with no onError fallback to the Package placeholder used for image-less items. Fixed: track image state (lifecycle or onError) and show the placeholder until the file exists.

## Flow
- Add Item "Frost Blade"
- card appears with imagePath /items/frost-blade.webp
- file does not exist yet -> broken image icon; CLI fails -> stays broken

## Expected impact
New items show the placeholder until their icon lands; measured by a render test firing onError on the image. Could hide a real misconfigured path behind a placeholder (log it).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - no broken image icons on catalog cards
Before: reproduced by reading: 1 of 1 just-added items renders a 404 image until the CLI finishes
After: predicted 0
Method: simulation - read both sites; the fix needs an image-state source (onError vs lifecycle), a small design choice
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: render TradingCard, fire error on the img, assert the Package placeholder renders

title: Move focus into the item detail drawer and back on close
body:
## Summary
Opening an item (click or Enter) mounts the detail drawer below the grid without moving focus to it; closing does not return focus to the card.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/catalog/ItemDetailDrawer.tsx:17-50 renders the panel and a Close button but never focuses anything; src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/catalog/CatalogItemGrid.tsx:48-51 toggles selection only. On a 20-card page the drawer opens off-screen below the grid and a keyboard user must tab through every card to reach it; Close drops focus to body. Fixed: focus the drawer heading on open, restore focus to the originating card on close.

## Flow
- focus a card with arrows, press Enter
- drawer opens below the grid; focus stays on the card
- press Close (after tabbing to it); focus goes to <body>

## Expected impact
Keyboard users land in the drawer and return to their card; measured by a render test on document.activeElement. Could scroll the page unexpectedly for mouse users (use preventScroll on mouse open).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the drawer is reachable and dismissable without losing place
Before: reproduced by reading: 0 focus moves on open, 0 on close
After: predicted 1 and 1
Method: simulation - read drawer + grid; needs the card ref threaded to the drawer (M across 3 files)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: RTL: press Enter on a card, assert activeElement is inside the drawer; click Close, assert activeElement is the card

title: Decide whether the Equipment Loadout is a persisted design artefact
body:
## Summary
The loadout visualizer equips items into component-local state keyed by name, so every loadout is lost on navigation and is not tied to catalog item ids.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/catalog/EquipmentLoadoutSection.tsx:99 seeds useState(LOADOUT_SLOTS) and handleSelect (:105-119) copies name/rarity/stats into the slot - no catalog id, no store, no persist. Since the picker now lists catalog items (d714c3b9), designers can equip real items, but the result evaporates and goes stale if the item is retuned. Whether the loadout should be a persisted, id-referencing artefact (and feed balance tooling) or stay a scratch preview is a product call.

## Flow
- equip 4 catalog items
- switch module tab and back (LRU suspend survives) or reload
- reload -> loadout back to the static LOADOUT_SLOTS seed

## Expected impact
Either the loadout becomes a durable design input or its scratch nature is stated in the UI. Could break nothing today; persistence adds a store migration.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - loadout is either persisted by id or labelled scratch
Before: by reading: 0 of 1 loadout states persisted; slots store copies, not ids
After: unmeasured - depends on the product decision
Method: simulation - read the component; the benefit depends on intended use, which no instrument settles
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
instrument: n/a - operator decision: persisted id-based loadout vs labelled scratch preview

title: Keep the trading-card tooltip inside the viewport on the last column
body:
## Summary
The trading-card stat tooltip always opens to the right (left-full ml-2, w-64), so on the rightmost grid column it renders past the viewport edge.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/catalog/TradingCardTooltip.tsx:19 positions the tooltip absolute left-full with a fixed 256px width; the grid is 4 columns at xl (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_inventory/catalog/CatalogItemGrid.tsx:39). Cards in column 4 push the tooltip off-screen (or under a scroll container). Fixed: flip to right-full when the card is in the last column (column index is known from columnCount) or use the shared tooltip positioning primitive.

## Flow
- viewport 1440px, 4-column grid
- hover a card in column 4
- tooltip renders mostly beyond the right edge

## Expected impact
Last-column tooltips are readable; measured by a browser probe of the tooltip bounding rect at 1280/1440. Could misplace tooltips if column detection drifts from the Tailwind breakpoints.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - tooltips stay on screen
Before: by reading: 1 of 4 columns (25% of cards at xl) opens the tooltip off-screen
After: predicted 0 of 4
Method: simulation - jsdom has no layout, so the figure needs a real-browser probe
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Playwright probe at 1440px: hover a column-4 card, assert tooltip rect.right <= viewport width
